title: Routine lane: no claim, lease, anchor, or window for routine changes
objective: Keep the Task Hall's checkpoint, claim, lease, anchor, and continuation machinery for coordinated, evidence-bearing, or rule-changing work, and let routine changes (documentation, tests, tooling, non-breaking package changes) enter through the start-here path with the merge-readiness verdict as the only gate.
current_question: Does exempting routine changes from the checkpoint machinery lose any accountability the repository needs, given that every routine change still carries an accountable GitHub identity, a changelog entry, the repository contract, and the verdict?

assumptions.statement: The maintainer and their Agent needed five round trips to land a routine change; an outside contributor faces the same cost plus the reading load of the Task Hall, which is a barrier the contribution route was not meant to be.
The rule took effect on 2026-09-16 by maintainer direction under the prototype principle of acting and keeping the undo; the introducing commit named in CHANGELOG.md is the undo.

options.summary: Routine changes skip claims, leases, anchors, continuation receipts, and windows; the verdict, changelog discipline, and a named identity are the accountability.
trade_offs: Ten-minute path for people and Agents
Two routine changes can collide on the same file; git and the verdict's conflict check resolve it after the fact instead of a lease preventing it

options.summary: Keep the claim and lease requirement for every change.
trade_offs: Keeps the entry fee that stopped the maintainer's own contributions

agreements: Non-routine work keeps the full checkpoint machinery under both options.
disagreements: Whether reservation is worth its cost for small changes is the open question.
missing_evidence: One outside contributor completing the start-here path end to end.

decision.summary: Routine changes (documentation, tests, tooling, non-breaking package changes) enter through the start-here path with the merge-readiness verdict as the only gate; claims, leases, anchors, continuation receipts, and windows stay for coordinated, evidence-bearing, and rule-changing work.
rationale: The governance_policy review window ran from 2026-09-16T14:00:00Z to 2026-09-23T14:00:00Z and closed with no risk or counterexample delta on the record.

Recorded under exact_next_action: with no objection delta at window close, the weekly steward records OPT-ROUTINE-LANE by lazy consensus under mandate.weekly-steward.v1, which was in force at decided_at.

Accountability for a routine change is the named GitHub identity, the changelog entry, the repository contract, and the verdict; the collision trade-off is resolved after the fact by git and the verdict's conflict check, which the record names as the accepted cost.
The missing evidence (one outside contributor completing the start-here path end to end) is milestone batch 1f's cold-start receipt (WI-010), not a precondition of this record.

scope: docs/contributing/start-here.md and merge-readiness.md stay as written: the routine lane needs no claim, lease, anchor, continuation receipt, or window.
docs/contributing/task-hall.md keeps the full checkpoint machinery for non-routine work; no edit is owed by this decision.

The execution checkpoint is tracked under the public-collaboration umbrella Issue #64 because the mandate forbids the steward from creating an Issue; a maintainer may re-point task to a dedicated Issue without reopening this record.
non_goals: No change to claims, leases, or continuation receipts for non-routine work.
execution.exact_next_action: Resolved by lazy consensus with OPT-ROUTINE-LANE. Nothing to edit: the routine lane already exists as written. The follow-up evidence (an outside contributor's cold-start receipt) is WI-010 under Issue #64; a person who finds a routine change that needed a lease opens a successor record with the counterexample.

reopen_conditions: Two routine changes collide in a way the verdict did not catch before merge.
A routine change collides with coordinated work in a way git and the verdict's conflict check did not catch; a successor record carries the counterexample.
